_: Copy to cloud.json and edit. cloud.json is NOT committed: it holds an account id, a domain, a Google client id and other people's email addresses, and this repository is public. Keys starting with _ are ignored, so these lines can stay. Nothing here is a secret in the cryptographic sense -- the one actual secret, the Google OAuth client secret, is never stored at all: it is passed as a NoEcho CloudFormation parameter at deploy time and re-entered on each deploy.
__aws: Where it deploys. Everything is us-east-1: Lambda@Edge and ACM certificates must live there, so using one region throughout removes every cross-region stack reference. profile is a named ~/.aws profile -- credentials never sit in this tree.
__site: The public face. domain must be a SUBDOMAIN, not an apex: it is pointed at CloudFront with a CNAME, which is illegal at a zone apex, and using a subdomain is what keeps the parent zone's own records -- MX especially -- untouched. You add that CNAME by hand at whatever registrar holds the parent.
__cert: The ACM certificate, created OUT OF BAND and referenced by ARN -- see cloud/README.md for why a CloudFormation resource that blocks on someone editing DNS in a browser is the worse option. Must be us-east-1: CloudFront can attach a certificate from nowhere else.
__capture: The capture host's timezone, as an IANA name. The archive's filenames, heartbeats and axis labels are all in the capture host's local clock, and series.tz_runs() reads time.localtime() -- so the ingest Lambda runs with TZ set to this, or it would label the data in UTC. Tiles themselves are partitioned on UTC boundaries regardless; only the labels are local.
__auth: Google sign-in, via a Cognito user pool with Google as the identity provider. allowed_emails is the read allowlist, checked in the viewer-request Lambda@Edge against the verified id token's email claim -- Cognito will authenticate any Google account, so this list is what actually gates the site. auth_domain_prefix must be globally unique and may not contain 'aws', 'amazon' or 'cognito'.
__google_redirect: Register ONE authorized redirect URI on the Google OAuth client, and it is NOT this site -- it is the Cognito Hosted UI: https://<auth_domain_prefix>.auth.<region>.amazoncognito.com/oauth2/idpresponse . Google redirects to Cognito, which then redirects to https://<domain>/auth/callback; that second URL is set by the CDK on the app client and is not a Google setting. Registering it with Google instead gives 'Error 400: redirect_uri_mismatch' on every sign-in, and Google's error details name the idpresponse URI it expected. `cdk deploy SigenAuthPool` prints both as GoogleAuthorizedRedirectUri and CognitoCallbackUrl. Also check the consent screen's Publishing status: while it is 'Testing' only accounts on its Test users list can sign in, whatever allowed_emails says.
__pool: Filled in AFTER `cdk deploy SigenAuthPool`, from its UserPoolId and ClientId outputs. Leave them empty on a first deploy: SigenAuthEdge and SigenSite do not even appear in `cdk ls` until both are set, which is deliberate -- a Lambda@Edge cannot be given them as environment variables, so they are baked into its code at synth, and synthesizing before the pool exists would bake a CloudFormation token and reject every valid login.
